feature_results.rationale: GitHub Copilot documents a hooks mechanism (docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/hooks, and CLI/coding-agent specific pages) that runs user-supplied shell commands at multiple defined lifecycle points across the agent's action lifecycle: sessionStart, sessionEnd, userPromptSubmitted, preToolUse, postToolUse, agentStop, and subagentStop. The preToolUse hook can return a permission decision that approves or denies (blocks) the tool call before it runs, satisfying the requirement that hooks be able to influence/block an action, not just passively observe it. Coverage spans pre/post tool-call events generally, not a single narrow event type, so this is not merely partial.

evidence.excerpt: Hooks are a way of executing custom shell commands at strategic points in an agent's workflow, such as when an agent session starts or ends, when you enter a prompt, or when a tool is called.
preToolUse: Executed before the agent uses any tool (such as bash, edit, view). This is the most powerful hook as it can approve or deny tool executions.

constraints.description: Hook configuration files must be committed to the repository (e.g. .github/hooks/*.json, on the default branch for Coding Agent) to take effect; they are repository-scoped rather than a global user setting.

queries: GitHub Copilot coding agent custom instructions hooks pre-commit hook agent lifecycle
"About hooks for GitHub Copilot" preToolUse postToolUse permissionDecision sessionStart docs.github.com

feature_results.rationale: GitHub Copilot coding agent documentation describes a configurable firewall governing the agent's execution environment: a 'recommended allowlist' of common OS package repos, container registries, and language package registries is enabled by default, and administrators can customize (add/remove entries) or fully disable this allowlist, with the full set of allowlisted hosts documented in a dedicated allowlist reference. This is a documented, configurable outbound-network restriction specific to agent execution (distinct from general sandbox/process isolation), satisfying has_criteria.

evidence.excerpt: The firewall always allows access to a number of hosts that Copilot uses to interact with GitHub, and by default, a recommended allowlist is also enabled to allow the agent to download dependencies.
Disabling the recommended allowlist is likely to increase the risk of unauthorized access to external resources.

constraints.description: The firewall only applies to processes started by the agent via its Bash tool during coding-agent sessions; it does not apply to Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers or to processes started in configured Copilot setup steps, and it only operates within the GitHub Actions appliance environment used to run the coding agent.

feature_results.rationale: GitHub Copilot CLI documents a session-wide rollback ('rewind') mechanism: Copilot takes a workspace snapshot at the start of each prompt, and the user can restore the whole workspace (not just one file/hunk) to an earlier point in the session via the /undo (/rewind) slash command or by pressing Esc twice. This restores session-wide state in one operation, matching the has_criteria.

evidence.excerpt: If Copilot has already made changes and you want to undo them, you can roll back your workspace to a previous point in the session.
You can trigger a rewind by pressing Esc twice, or by using the /undo slash command (or its alias /rewind).

constraints.description: Rewinding cannot be undone: once rolled back, later session history is permanently removed, and files over 10 MB are skipped during snapshot creation so changes to them are not restored during a rollback.
The documented rollback/rewind mechanism applies to GitHub Copilot CLI sessions.

queries: GitHub Copilot coding agent session checkpoint rollback undo

feature_results.rationale: GitHub documents a dedicated Copilot code review workflow: a reviewer can be requested on a pull request (or configured to run automatically), and Copilot posts a Comment-type review with feedback and, where possible, suggested changes. This is a documented, dedicated review/PR workflow, not just ad-hoc chat, and it also integrates with a hosting platform (GitHub.com), so it meets the has_criteria and exceeds the partial_criteria bar (local-diff-only).

evidence.excerpt: GitHub Copilot can review your code and provide feedback, and where possible, Copilot's feedback includes suggested changes which you can apply with a couple of clicks.
Copilot always leaves a "Comment" review, not an "Approve" or "Request changes" review, and its reviews do not count toward required approvals and will not block merging.

You can configure Copilot code review to review pull requests automatically. You can select the effort level for automatic reviews, with "Low" providing standard review (default) and "Medium" providing deeper analysis of complex logic, security-sensitive code, and cross-service changes.

constraints.description: Copilot code review is a premium feature available with the Copilot Pro, Copilot Pro+, Copilot Business, and Copilot Enterprise plans.

feature_results.rationale: GitHub officially documents a supported way for customers to point Copilot at their own local/self-hosted model instead of GitHub's cloud-hosted model. GitHub Copilot CLI supports 'Bring Your Own Key' (BYOK), explicitly including locally running models such as Ollama, vLLM, and Foundry Local, configured via environment variables pointing at a local endpoint; an offline mode (COPILOT_OFFLINE=true) stops the CLI contacting GitHub's servers entirely when combined with a local model. The GitHub Copilot desktop app separately documents the same BYOK mechanism for agent sessions, including Ollama and LM Studio as local providers. This is not limited to a narrow feature subset (e.g. completions only) -- it covers full agent/chat sessions with tool-calling models -- so it meets has_criteria rather than partial_criteria.

additional_facts.description: GitHub Copilot ships a distinctly named, built-in "plan agent" mode alongside its general chat/agent mode: the plan agent explores the codebase using only read-only tools, asks clarifying questions, and drafts a plan for the user to review and refine before any files are touched -- unlike agent mode, it does not edit files or run implementation steps while planning. Separately, developers can author their own named custom sub-agents (.agent.md Markdown files with YAML frontmatter defining a name, prompt, and tool-access scope); the parent Copilot runtime automatically delegates a matching request to the appropriate custom agent, running it in an isolated context while streaming lifecycle events back to the parent session. Copilot CLI additionally exposes a /fleet slash command that dispatches multiple such sub-agents to work simultaneously on independent tasks.

evidence.excerpt: The plan agent explores your codebase by using read-only tools, asks clarifying questions when needed, and drafts a plan that you can review and refine. Unlike agent mode, the plan agent doesn't edit files or run implementation steps while you're planning.

When a user's request matches an agent's expertise, the Copilot runtime automatically delegates to that agent as a sub-agent—running it in an isolated context while streaming lifecycle events back to the parent session.
/fleet is a slash command in Copilot CLI that enables Copilot to simultaneously work with multiple subagents in parallel

use_cases.title: AI-assisted first-pass pull request review with static-analysis findings
use_cases.description: A maintainer requests (or configures automatic) Copilot code review on a pull request; Copilot leaves a Comment-type review with feedback and, where possible, suggested changes, incorporating results from CodeQL, ESLint, and PMD directly into its feedback so lint/static-analysis findings surface as part of the same AI-driven review rather than a separate manual pass.

evidence.excerpt: GitHub Copilot can review your code and provide feedback, and where possible, Copilot's feedback includes suggested changes which you can apply with a couple of clicks.

In addition to CodeQL quality detections... you can now get results from ESLint (which highlights issues for JavaScript and TypeScript projects) and PMD (which scans for problems in Java, Apex, and other supported languages).

use_cases.title: Assign a Dependabot security alert to Copilot for automated remediation
use_cases.description: When Dependabot flags a vulnerable dependency, a maintainer assigns the resulting alert directly to Copilot, which analyzes the vulnerability advisory and opens a draft pull request with a proposed fix for review.

evidence.excerpt: You can now assign Dependabot alerts to AI coding agents, including Copilot, Claude, and Codex, to analyze the vulnerability and open a draft pull request with a proposed fix.

use_cases.title: Governed enterprise-wide rollout with regional data controls and layered instructions
use_cases.description: A regulated enterprise could roll out Copilot organization-wide while enforcing SAML SSO-based access, requiring Copilot inference to stay within an approved US or EU region, and layering organization-wide coding-convention instructions beneath repository- and personal-level custom instructions -- combining several independently documented enterprise controls into a single governance-oriented deployment.
use_cases.rationale: enterprise_sso_access_control, data_processing_region_control, and layered_instruction_precedence are each documented independently as separate Copilot/GitHub Enterprise controls; combining them into a single 'controlled enterprise rollout' narrative is a reasonable synthesis rather than a single official page's description of one named workflow.

use_cases.title: Run Copilot CLI unattended inside a CI/CD pipeline
use_cases.description: A GitHub Actions workflow (or other automated pipeline) invokes the standalone copilot CLI non-interactively via the -p/--prompt flag, with prompts for additional input suppressed, so the CLI exits automatically once its task completes and its response is captured in the job log without a human present to respond to any prompts.

evidence.excerpt: Use copilot -p PROMPT [OPTIONS] to run the CLI programmatically and exit when the command completes.
which is important when running in an automated workflow where there is no user to respond to requests for additional input

use_cases.title: Delegate a GitHub issue to Copilot's coding agent for autonomous implementation
use_cases.description: A developer assigns a GitHub Issue to Copilot from github.com, GitHub Mobile, or the CLI; the coding/cloud agent works independently in its own ephemeral cloud sandbox, creates a branch, edits code across files, runs tests and linters, and continues running in the background even after the requester's own machine is off, before opening a pull request for human review.

evidence.excerpt: The Copilot cloud agent can pick up a task from an issue, a pull request comment, or Copilot Chat, create a branch, generate tailored code changes, and open a pull request.
runs in the cloud, can work in parallel on multiple tasks, and continues even if your computer is off

use_cases.title: Fan a large mechanical backlog out across many parallel Copilot tasks
use_cases.description: A team could dispatch a batch of similar, independent chores -- dependency bumps, lint fixups, or repeated migration steps across several repositories -- to the coding agent at once via the agents panel, or to several Copilot CLI sub-agents via /fleet, so the batch completes in parallel in the background rather than being worked through one task at a time.
use_cases.rationale: This combines three independently documented capabilities -- the coding agent's parallel, multi-task 'agents panel' workflow, Copilot CLI's /fleet parallel sub-agent dispatch, and the coding agent's background/asynchronous execution -- into a single 'clear a backlog in parallel' narrative that no single official source describes as one named, end-to-end workflow.

use_cases.title: Turn a design mockup or screenshot into working code
use_cases.description: A developer attaches a screenshot, mockup, diagram, or PDF directly to a Copilot chat prompt; Copilot Vision reasons about the attached image alongside the surrounding code and generates a corresponding implementation.

evidence.excerpt: Copilot Vision is now generally available, allowing you to attach images and PDFs directly to your chat prompts so Copilot can reason about what it sees alongside your code.
